description: A study of English tenses including simple present, present continuous, simple past, past continuous, simple future, the 'going to' future and basic present perfect, with correct verb forms and matching time expressions.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct sentence in the simple present tense.

options.text: She walk to school every morning.
She walks to school every morning.
She walking to school every morning.
She is walk to school every morning.

mcq.explanation: In the simple present, verbs take -s with third person singular subjects like 'she', so the form is 'walks'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence is in the present continuous tense?

options.text: The children play in the yard daily.
The children played in the yard.
The children are playing in the yard now.
The children will play in the yard.

mcq.explanation: The present continuous uses 'am/is/are' plus the -ing form to show an action happening now.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct simple past form: Yesterday Maria _____ a long letter to her cousin.
mcq.explanation: The time word 'yesterday' signals a finished past action, so the irregular simple past 'wrote' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the past continuous tense?

options.text: I was cooking when the lights went off.
I cook when the lights went off.
I am cooking when the lights went off.
I will cook when the lights went off.

mcq.explanation: The past continuous ('was/were' + -ing) describes an action in progress in the past, often interrupted by another past action.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct simple future sentence.

options.text: We visit our grandmother next week.
We will visit our grandmother next week.
We visited our grandmother next week.
We are visit our grandmother next week.

mcq.explanation: The simple future is formed with 'will' plus the base verb, and 'next week' shows future time.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence uses the 'going to' future to show a plan?

options.text: Joseph goes to open a shop next month.
Joseph is going to open a shop next month.
Joseph opened a shop next month.
Joseph opens a shop next month.

mcq.explanation: The structure 'am/is/are going to' + base verb expresses a plan or intention for the future.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct present perfect sentence.

options.text: I have finished my homework already.
I has finished my homework already.
I have finish my homework already.
I finished have my homework already.

mcq.explanation: The present perfect uses 'have/has' plus the past participle; with 'I' we use 'have finished'.

mcq.questionText: Which time expression best fits the simple present tense?
mcq.explanation: The simple present describes habits and routines, so it pairs with expressions like 'every day', 'always' and 'usually'.

mcq.questionText: Identify the tense: 'The farmers were harvesting maize all afternoon.'
mcq.explanation: The form 'were harvesting' ('were' + -ing) marks the past continuous, showing an action in progress over a period in the past.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb form: Look! The bus _____ at the stop now.
mcq.explanation: The words 'Look!' and 'now' show an action happening at this moment, which needs the present continuous 'is stopping'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct in the simple past?

options.text: They did not went to the market.
They did not go to the market.
They not went to the market.
They does not go to the market yesterday.

mcq.explanation: In negative past sentences we use 'did not' followed by the base verb, so the correct form is 'did not go'.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct question form in the present continuous.
mcq.explanation: In present continuous questions the form of 'be' comes before the subject: 'What are you doing?'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence uses 'will' to make a sudden decision?

options.text: It is raining; I will close the window.
It is raining; I closed the window.
It is raining; I close the window.
It is raining; I was closing the window.

mcq.explanation: We often use 'will' for a decision made at the moment of speaking, such as deciding to close a window because of rain.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct present perfect sentence with 'since'.

options.text: She has lived in Mwanza since 2019.
She is living in Mwanza since 2019.

mcq.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues to now uses the present perfect, and 'since' marks the starting point: 'has lived since 2019'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence correctly combines a past continuous and a simple past action?

options.text: While she read, the phone rang.
While she was reading, the phone rang.
While she was reading, the phone was ringing.
While she reads, the phone rang.

mcq.explanation: The longer background action takes the past continuous ('was reading') and the short interrupting action takes the simple past ('rang').

fib.questionText: Every Sunday my father _____ (wash) his bicycle.
fib.explanation: The habit word 'every Sunday' needs the simple present, and with 'my father' the verb adds -es to become 'washes'.

fib.questionText: Right now the baby _____ (sleep) in the cradle.
fib.explanation: 'Right now' shows an action in progress, so we use the present continuous 'is sleeping'.

fib.questionText: Last week we _____ (buy) new uniforms for the term.
fib.explanation: 'Last week' marks finished past time, so the irregular simple past of 'buy' is 'bought'.

fib.questionText: When the teacher entered, the pupils _____ (talk) loudly.
fib.explanation: The action was already in progress when another past action happened, so the past continuous 'were talking' is used.

fib.questionText: Tomorrow our class _____ (have) a debate about the environment.
fib.explanation: 'Tomorrow' points to the future, so we use 'will' plus the base verb to form 'will have'.

fib.questionText: We have packed our bags because we _____ (travel) to Dodoma this evening.
fib.explanation: A planned future action is expressed with 'am/is/are going to', giving 'are going to travel'.

fib.questionText: I _____ (already / eat) my lunch, so I am not hungry.
fib.explanation: The present perfect 'have' plus the past participle 'eaten' shows a recently completed action, with 'already' placed in the middle.

fib.questionText: She _____ (not / understand) the question, so she asked the teacher.
fib.explanation: A negative simple past uses 'did not' plus the base verb, giving 'did not understand'.
'Listen!' signals an action happening at this moment, so the present continuous 'is knocking' is correct.

fib.questionText: My uncle _____ (work) at the hospital since January.
fib.explanation: An action starting in the past and continuing to now uses the present perfect with 'since', giving 'has worked'.

tf.questionText: The simple present tense is used to talk about habits and things that are generally true.
tf.explanation: Habits, routines and general facts such as 'Water boils at 100 degrees' are expressed in the simple present.

tf.questionText: The present continuous tense is formed by adding -ing directly to the base verb without any helping verb.
tf.explanation: The present continuous needs a form of 'be' (am, is, are) before the -ing verb, for example 'is running'.

tf.questionText: The word 'yesterday' usually goes with the simple past tense.
tf.explanation: 'Yesterday' refers to a finished past time, so it pairs with the simple past, as in 'arrived yesterday'.

tf.questionText: All English verbs form the simple past by adding -ed.
tf.explanation: Many irregular verbs change their form instead of adding -ed, such as 'go' becoming 'went' and 'see' becoming 'saw'.

tf.questionText: The past continuous tense often describes a longer action that was interrupted by a shorter past action.
tf.explanation: We use the past continuous for the background action and the simple past for the interrupting action, as in 'was cooking when she called'.

tf.questionText: Both 'will' and 'going to' can be used to talk about the future.
tf.explanation: 'Will' often shows decisions or predictions, while 'going to' shows plans, but both refer to future time.

tf.questionText: In the present perfect tense, the verb 'have' is always used, never 'has'.
tf.explanation: We use 'has' with third person singular subjects (he, she, it) and 'have' with other subjects.

tf.questionText: The time expression 'now' fits well with the present continuous tense.
tf.explanation: 'Now' shows an action happening at the moment of speaking, which is the meaning of the present continuous.

tf.questionText: In a negative simple past sentence we say 'did not went'.
tf.explanation: After 'did not' we use the base form of the verb, so the correct sentence is 'did not go'.

tf.questionText: 'Since' and 'for' are commonly used with the present perfect tense.
tf.explanation: We use 'since' for a starting point and 'for' for a length of time, as in 'since Monday' or 'for three years'.

summary.questionText: How is the simple present formed with third person singular subjects?
summary.correctAnswer: Add -s or -es to the base verb (he plays, she watches).
summary.explanation: Third person singular subjects he, she and it take an -s or -es ending in the simple present.

summary.questionText: What is the structure of the present continuous tense?
summary.explanation: It combines a present form of 'be' with the -ing form to show an action happening now.

summary.questionText: How do regular verbs form the simple past?
summary.correctAnswer: Add -ed to the base verb (walk - walked).
summary.explanation: Most regular verbs add -ed, while irregular verbs change form instead.

summary.questionText: What is the structure of the past continuous tense?
summary.explanation: It shows an action that was in progress at a particular time in the past.

summary.questionText: How is the simple future tense formed?
summary.explanation: The simple future uses 'will' followed by the base form of the verb.

summary.questionText: What does the 'going to' future express?
summary.correctAnswer: A plan or intention: am/is/are going to + base verb.
summary.explanation: It is used for future actions that are already planned or decided.

summary.questionText: What is the structure of the present perfect tense?
summary.explanation: It links a past action to the present, often with words like 'already', 'just', 'since' and 'for'.

summary.questionText: Which time expressions usually go with the simple present?
summary.explanation: These expressions describe how often a habit or routine happens.

summary.questionText: How do we form negatives and questions in the simple past?
summary.explanation: The helper 'did' carries the past tense, so the main verb stays in its base form.

summary.questionText: Which time words signal future time?
summary.explanation: These expressions show that an action will happen after the present moment.

hoq.questionText: Rewrite in the most natural tense: 'I _____ (study) for two hours before my friend arrived, but I was still tired.' Choose the best option.
hoq.explanation: An action completed before another past action uses the past perfect 'had studied', showing it happened before the friend arrived.

hoq.questionText: Which sentence correctly fixes the tense error in 'When I will see her tomorrow, I will give her the book.'?

options.text: When I see her tomorrow, I will give her the book.
When I will see her tomorrow, I give her the book.
When I saw her tomorrow, I will give her the book.
When I will seeing her tomorrow, I will give her the book.

hoq.explanation: After time words like 'when' we use the simple present for the future, not 'will', so 'When I see her tomorrow' is correct.

hoq.questionText: Choose the sentence that correctly distinguishes a finished time from an unfinished time.

options.text: I have visited Arusha last year.
I visited Arusha last year, and I have visited it again this year.
I visited Arusha this year, and I have visited it last year.
I have visit Arusha last year and this year.

hoq.explanation: A finished time like 'last year' takes the simple past, while an unfinished time like 'this year' takes the present perfect.
